tasks.short: Determine severity from stored threat counts

steps.what: Load incident counts by threat type
Draft vulnerability analyses from stored counts

loop.purpose: Draft vulnerability analyses that cite only stored threat counts.
loop.input: Threat type id and incident count for the period.
loop.output: Analysis lines that each cite a threat type id.
loop.check: Every line cites a stored count, and no severity is added.
loop.stop: Stop when the period has no counts.
loop.why_not_simpler: A matrix cannot show which count a line came from.

tasks.design: Incident counts by threat type are loaded on {BI}. A draft analysis cites only those counts. The security manager determines severity and consequence. A count is not a severity.
tasks.previous_blocker: Threat tables were rebuilt by hand before each review.
tasks.enabler_now: Counts can be queried by threat type and period.
tasks.still_hard: Severity, criticality, and the effect on delivery stay a determination.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which count is not the risk that matters.

ambition.what: A closed period can be analysed the same week, and a draft with no counts is not filed.

tasks.altitude: The week is the severity decision, not the recount.

evidence.claim: The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person. Counts can be listed. Severity is not a formula in the source pack.

assumptions: The work starts when a review period closes and ends when the manager files the severity decision.
A count has a threat type id, a period, and an integer, produced by the incident log. A type with no rows is shown as zero only if the log confirms zero.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether incidents are already coded by threat type.
research_questions: Who sets what counts as a severe consequence for this firm?

already_counted.description: Determining severity is already in the decision step.

incremental.description: Retire an analysis when a count is corrected.

approvals.approved_version: severity the manager determined for that period

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when threat types are not coded. Severity stays a determination. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine the property against security policies

steps.what: List the physical examinations still due
Conduct the examinations on the property

tasks.design: Due physical examinations are listed from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Conducting them on the property stays with the security manager. Compliance with security policies is noted from what was seen, not from the due list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due walks were a paper rota, and findings were retyped later.
tasks.enabler_now: A due list can show which place has not been walked.
tasks.still_hard: The examination itself, and whether it complies, stays on the property.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sees a gap the last note did not mention.
tasks.altitude: The due list is current. The walk and the compliance note stay in person.

reach.task: Fix a gap the examination noted

evidence.claim: The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person. A due list does not examine a building.

assumptions: The work starts when an examination falls due and ends when the manager notes compliance.
A due row has a place id and a date, produced by the last examination. A place with no row is not marked examined.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether examination dates are already stored by place.
research_questions: Which policies each place is checked against?

already_counted.description: The walk is already in the examination step.

incremental.description: Reopen a note if the place changes after the walk.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when due dates are paper. The examination stays on the property. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide compliance of security policies and programs

steps.what: Compare stored procedures with government requirements
Draft gaps against internal security policies

loop.purpose: Draft gaps that cite only stored policies and requirements.
loop.input: Policy id and requirement id with their dates.
loop.output: Gap lines that cite both ids.
loop.check: Every line cites a stored policy and a stored requirement.
loop.stop: Stop when either id is missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A date compare alone cannot explain the gap in words the manager will use.

tasks.design: Procedure dates are compared with stored government requirements. A draft gap cites internal security policies and those requirements. The security manager decides compliance with the directives. A date gap is not a breach.
tasks.previous_blocker: Compliance was a periodic reread of two binders.
tasks.enabler_now: Policies and requirements can be stored with dates and ids.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a program complies stays a decision.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows a directive the date compare does not capture.

ambition.what: A changed requirement can be compared the same week, and an unchecked gap is not filed as a breach.

tasks.altitude: The week is the compliance decision, not the search for the current text.

evidence.claim: Comparing stored dates is deterministic. The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person. Compliance is still decided by a person.

assumptions: The work starts when policies or requirements change and ends when the manager files the compliance decision.
A procedure and a requirement each have an id and a date, produced by the document store. A text that is not stored is not compared.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether government requirements are stored with stable ids.
research_questions: Which directives this firm treats as binding?

already_counted.description: The compliance decision is already in the decision step.

incremental.description: Retire a gap when a policy date changes.

approvals.approved_version: compliance decision the manager made for those ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when requirements are not stored. A date gap is not filed as a breach. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assemble stored facts for the agency
Coordinate security operations with public enforcement
Send the agreed note to the agency

tasks.design: Stored incident facts are assembled from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Coordinating operations with public enforcement, fire, and other agencies stays a conversation. Only the note the manager agreed is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency calls started from memory, and the follow-up mail drifted.
tasks.enabler_now: Incident facts can be assembled before the call.
tasks.still_hard: What to tell an agency, and what was agreed, stays the manager's.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows what must not leave the firm.
tasks.altitude: The call starts from a facts pack. Nothing is sent until the manager agrees the note.

reach.learn: What was agreed and what was withheld

evidence.claim: The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person. Sending a note outside the firm waits for the manager.

assumptions: The work starts when an agency coordination is needed and ends when the agreed note is sent.
A fact has an incident id and a text the manager has already marked shareable. An unmarked fact is not put in the pack.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Which facts the firm is allowed to send to which agency.
research_questions: Is fire coordination a different path from law enforcement?

already_counted.description: The call is already in the coordination step.

incremental.description: Correct a sent note if the agreement was mis-recorded.

approvals.approved_version: note the manager agreed for that agency

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when facts are not stored. The call stays. An unmarked fact is not sent. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Threat counts are not a severity. Property examinations stay physical. A compliance gap is filed only after the manager decides. Agency notes leave only when the manager agrees.
reach: The director sees the filed severity, not the count.
An agency receives only the agreed note.
skills_to_grow: Do not treat a zero count as proof nothing happened.
Do not send a fact the manager did not mark.
role.ambitious_version: A changed requirement is compared the same week, and an unchecked gap is not called a breach.
